<reason>B won with a cleaner live decision rule: after notice, basic exclusion is either priced or permitted, and CON’s softer tools leave it cheap. A landed a real mechanism attack—platform exit, small-org harm, and injunctions targeting the pathway rather than the wallet—that B never fully killed, but A never named a non-fine cost that prices delay on ordinary public doors. B stayed tighter to “basic/repeated,” answered pressure more directly, and made the vote easier.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s Q1 (what non-fine cost makes a still-broken form more expensive than repair) forced A into lawsuits/procurement/injunctions, which B then weighed as lottery, limited coverage, or equivalent shutdown—leaving the pricing claim standing.</best_rebuttal>
